Here is a 5-paragraph summary of the article:

Former Liberal minister Philip Ruddock has been appointed by the Australian cabinet to review whether Australian law adequately protects the human right to religious freedom. The appointment was announced on Wednesday by Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull.

***

The move is intended to ease tensions over potential religious amendments to a same-sex marriage bill, following the recent "yes" vote on marriage equality. However, Treasurer Scott Morrison made clear that the review was "no substitute" for including religious amendments in the marriage bill itself.

***

There is a divide among senior conservatives about the timing of addressing religious freedom protections. While figures like Peter Dutton and Mathias Cormann believe a religious freedom bill can be addressed next year, separately from the marriage bill, Morrison and Liberal senator David Fawcett insist it should be considered at the same time.

***

Ruddock has been asked to deliver his report by 31 March. Turnbull noted that many proposals for legislative changes to protect religious freedom go beyond the immediate issue of marriage, and urged parliament to be cautious in considering them.

***

Turnbull warned of a "high risk of unintended consequences" when parliament attempts to legislate protections for basic rights, expressing particular concern about broadly worded, bill of rights-style declarations. He said Ruddock was well-suited for the role given his experience as Australia's special envoy for human rights.
